claim: The character-art equivalent of lens choice: hairline reads delicate and expensive, thick reads punchy and shounen, rough_genga reads like the key animation was shot before cleanup. It is the first thing the eye registers about a drawing.
method: identical subject sentence and seed in every panel; only the option clause changes. panels marked control render the untouched subject, because SDXL cannot express absence.

panels.clause: tapered lineart, varying line weight, expressive lines
brush stroke lineart, inked brush lines

review.issue: hairline ("extremely thin lineart, hairline outlines") and thin ("thin lineart, delicate outlines") will render identically - the model has one "thin lineart" feature and no degree control on it. Separately, rough_genga ("rough sketch, unfinished lineart, genga") is the same render as shot.fx.impact_frame/sketch_frame ("rough sketch, genga, pencil lines, unfinished drawing"); "rough sketch" dominates both.
review.fix: Drop hairline (or fold it into thin). For rough_genga, let line_weight own it and change impact_frame/sketch_frame to something that reads as a one-frame intrusion rather than a whole-drawing style - e.g. "rough sketch, monochrome, high contrast" - or accept the duplication and cut one.
